I've been to dozens of veterinary clinics, but I've been going to this one for the past 10 years or so.

While there are limitations to advanced medical care due to equipment limitations, it's truly excellent for a local clinic.

They're also quick to refer patients to other specialist hospitals when necessary.

We've been going to this clinic for a long time, and sadly, one of our pets passed away, but I'm incredibly grateful for the sincere care of the clinic director until the very end, and for the staff who tearfully saw our pet off.

We've continued to go there even after welcoming a new pet.

It's the go-to veterinary clinic in the area.

When I see negative reviews, it's always from people who just walked in or ended up with a less-than-satisfactory outcome.

I understand their feelings, but frankly, every hospital has its limitations and can have miscalculations.

The important thing is how much they support you.

If pet owners trust the doctor and treat them with sincerity, that will be conveyed. Ultimately, it's about human connection.

The idea that "the customer is always right" is a thing of the Showa era.

I think people with a complaining temperament and who always blame others will be the same no matter where they go.

At least we can confidently recommend this animal hospital.

Please do go and check it out.

The head veterinarian here doesn't actually treat animals; he's just managing appointments. Even in serious, life-threatening situations, he doesn't bother to explain things carefully, consider the cause, or show any empathy.

In fact, the more serious the situation, the more dismissive he becomes, as if it's too much trouble.

* Despite monthly checkups and continuous weight loss for several months, he dismissed it as "just old age," overlooking a serious illness.

* Even after receiving medication, my pet continued to vomit daily. I contacted him via LINE during clinic hours, but he read the message and ignored it. He left me hanging until I called him the next day.

* He didn't provide any information about the results of the externally ordered tests until a week later, when I had to repeatedly ask for them. (It only improved after I complained to the nurse.)

* In the end, his attitude was as if to say, "I've referred you to a secondary care facility, so don't come back."

How can he treat animals he's treated for years with such coldness? Does he have no heart?

I deeply regret ever being involved with this veterinarian.

As others have mentioned, this hospital prioritizes appointments over sick children.

* Although they specialize in kidneys, they basically only perform blood and urine tests and prescribe medication. They don't even take images unless requested.

* They only answer questions about important aspects of kidney management such as diet, supplements, and blood pressure; they don't offer proactive guidance.

* They ask you to register for their LINE account, but don't expect detailed follow-up.

Thank you so much for saving my cat's life so many times.
This time, it started with my cat vomiting, and I had a bad feeling that something was wrong, so I didn't hesitate to make an appointment for the next day and take her to the emergency vet.
The emergency vet examined her very well and said that it would be best to perform abdominal surgery to insert a nephrostomy tube, so I took her to our regular vet, Hanegi Animal Hospital, first thing in the morning.
Despite the difficult situation, the head vet managed to insert the nephrostomy tube without abdominal surgery.
It was very thorough, and the emergency vet had said that inserting a nephrostomy tube without abdominal surgery would be difficult and impossible in this situation, so I thought the head vet's technique was incredibly advanced.
Afterward, Dr. Okada was very kind and explained various options during her hospitalizations and discharges, which eased my anxieties.
I think this hospital is wonderful because it not only cares for the animals but also for the emotional well-being of the owners.
Thank you so much to all the doctors, nurses, and reception staff who took care of us this time.
Thank you to the nurse who spoke to me with a smile when I was discharged.

My cat had blood in her urine this evening, and when I tried to take her to our regular vet, unfortunately, it was closed. I searched for a hospital that was still open and called this one, but they told me, "We accept patients until 6:30 PM, but we only have one veterinarian, so we can't accept you. We'll direct you to the emergency center." (I called at 6:15 PM) I knew the emergency center didn't accept patients until 8:00 PM. I called this hospital because I wanted my cat to be seen as quickly as possible, so I'm disappointed. My family (my cat) is important to me, so I won't be using this hospital again in the future. I'm glad I found out the true nature of this hospital early on.

This hospital saved my beloved cat's life, and we now continue to visit them for treatment. I am so grateful for the thorough examinations and tests they provide each time.

The doctors here are very caring and always inform us if the condition is serious; they are truly trustworthy. Thank you so much, Dr. O.

My dog's condition worsened late that night on the day I visited this clinic, and I'm still dissatisfied with the treatment and handling, so I'm editing my original review and reposting it.

This is my second visit to this clinic since moving, and I came in because my dog ​​had severe diarrhea (bloody stools, about 10 times a day) for the past few days.

I didn't specifically request a veterinarian; I just wanted to have him examined because I was worried.

The first time I saw him was for a rabies vaccination, and the male veterinarian was very thorough and good.

This time, it was a female veterinarian. My first impression was good, but as we talked about the history of his symptoms, I felt like she was taking everything at face value, and she interrupted me a bit, so I couldn't ask many of the questions I wanted to. Also, I apologize if a medical record was properly written later, but no record was written during the examination, and I'm worried about whether my dog's condition will be properly handed over to the next veterinarian if it doesn't improve.

And what is the cause of this diarrhea? Even after asking questions, a clear diagnosis wasn't given. While it was partly my fault for not collecting a stool sample at home, I did explain that my dog's behavior and symptoms were clearly different from before.

Ultimately, they took my dog's temperature rectally and performed a test on a small amount of stool attached to the thermometer. The results were normal, and a probiotic was prescribed.

Regarding the prescription, since it was the day for my dog's heartworm medication prescription two days later, I tried to ask if it was okay to use them together, but they asked, "Hasn't your dog had its heartworm test yet?" (They took my word for heartworm at face value).

After all that, I went home.

Late that night, my dog's rectum protruded from its rear end, so I went to a different hospital. They performed a stool test, of course, but also a blood test.

The result was hemorrhagic colitis, causing my dog ​​to defecate more than 10 times a day, which had led to the prolapse.

Several days later, my dog ​​is now healthy thanks to the proper medication.

I acknowledge that I may have made some shortcomings as a pet owner, but despite clearly explaining the symptoms and emphasizing that it was clearly different from before, I am honestly shocked and angered by the inappropriate treatment given based solely on a simple stool test.

I'm sorry to say this, but I think the actions of one veterinarian can really shape the impression of an entire hospital.

I decided I never want to go there again.
The enthusiastic treatment here saved the life of my beloved dog who had pancreatitis and kidney disease. The veterinarians and nurses are also very kind and helpful. It's a wonderful hospital.

They were very kind and helpful with the insurance procedures. All the staff were very polite. They seem to be very serious about treatment, so I'm thinking of having my dogs examined there next time.

We sought a second opinion for our 13-year-old Shiba Inu with chronic kidney disease.

Based on the data from the approximately six months of treatment at our regular vet, we received comprehensive advice.

The diagnosis was very reassuring and satisfying. It was a very reassuring experience for us as pet owners. We are truly grateful.
